lessons.title: Classification
lessons.subtitle: Week 4: First milestone: explain an AI system
lessons.body:
Classification predicts a category. A classifier may output scores or probabilities before a category is selected. A predicted category can be wrong.

Offline practice: Classify eight fictional messages and note uncertain examples. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Classification predicts a category. A classifier may output scores or probabilities before a category is selected. A predicted category can be wrong.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Regression
lessons.subtitle: Week 4: First milestone: explain an AI system
lessons.body:
Regression predicts a numeric value, such as a journey duration. Predictions are estimates; they need error checks and realistic bounds.

Offline practice: Predict durations for three invented journeys and record the differences from supplied actual durations. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

lessons.title: Correlation and cause
lessons.subtitle: Week 4: First milestone: explain an AI system
lessons.body:
A relationship between two variables does not prove one causes the other. A third factor or coincidence may explain a pattern.

Offline practice: Write two possible explanations for a fictional relationship between library visits and examination results. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A relationship between two variables does not prove one causes the other. A third factor or coincidence may explain a pattern.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.

lessons.title: Explain limits clearly
lessons.subtitle: Week 4: First milestone: explain an AI system
lessons.body:
A clear explanation states the intended use, evidence, and limitations. Avoid claims that a model understands everything or is always correct.

Offline practice: Write a sixty-word explanation of a fictional classifier for someone new to AI. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A clear explanation states the intended use, evidence, and limitations. Avoid claims that a model understands everything or is always correct.

lessons.title: Month-one demonstration
lessons.subtitle: Week 4: First milestone: explain an AI system
lessons.body:
A demonstration should identify inputs, a learning method, outputs, an evaluation plan, and a human review step. A diagram can demonstrate understanding without coding.

Offline practice: Create a one-page AI-system diagram; explain one possible error and how a person would handle it. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A demonstration should identify inputs, a learning method, outputs, an evaluation plan, and a human review step. A diagram can demonstrate understanding without coding.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
